022import java.time.*;

030/**
031 * Token-bucket {@link RestGuard} that throttles requests on a configurable per-request key.
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * On each request the guard atomically attempts to acquire one token from a per-key bucket.  When tokens are
035 * available the request proceeds and three advisory response headers are populated
036 * ({@code X-RateLimit-Limit}, {@code X-RateLimit-Remaining}, {@code X-RateLimit-Reset}).  When the bucket is
037 * empty a {@link TooManyRequests} exception is thrown with a {@code Retry-After} header set to the integer
038 * number of seconds until the next token will be available.
039 *
040 * <h5 class='topic'>Example usage</h5>
041 *
042 * <p class='bjava'>
043 *    <ja>@Rest</ja>(path=<js>"/api"</js>)
044 *    <jk>public class</jk> ApiResource <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {
045 *
046 *       <jc>// Per-IP rate limit, 100 req/min, 200-burst.</jc>
047 *       <ja>@Bean</ja>(name=<js>"guards"</js>)
048 *       <jk>public</jk> RestGuardList rateLimits(BeanStore <jv>bs</jv>) {
049 *          <jk>return</jk> RestGuardList.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>bs</jv>)
050 *             .append(RateLimitGuard.<jsm>create</jsm>()
051 *                .permitsPerMinute(100)
052 *                .burst(200)
053 *                .build())
054 *             .build();
055 *       }
056 *    }
057 * </p>
058 *
059 * <h5 class='topic'>Keying</h5>
060 *
061 * <p>
062 * The default key is the request's {@linkplain RestRequest#getRemoteAddr() remote address}.  Set
063 * {@link Builder#xForwardedForAware(boolean) xForwardedForAware(true)} to honor the first hop of the
064 * {@code X-Forwarded-For} header — required when running behind a trusted reverse proxy.
065 *
066 * <p>
067 * <b>Trusted-proxy assumption.</b>  When {@code xForwardedForAware} is enabled without a trusted proxy in front
068 * of the application, attackers can spoof the {@code X-Forwarded-For} header and defeat the IP-based key.  Only
069 * opt in when the request edge enforces the header.
070 *
071 * <h5 class='topic'>Storage</h5>
072 *
073 * <p>
074 * Bucket state is held by a pluggable {@link Storage} SPI.  The default {@link Storage#inMemory()} implementation
075 * uses a {@link ConcurrentHashMap} with an LRU-style eviction policy (capped at 100 000 keys by default), suitable
076 * for single-pod deployments.  Distributed deployments should provide a substrate-backed implementation
077 * (e.g. Redis) so per-pod buckets do not split the shared rate envelope.
078 *
079 * <h5 class='topic'>Probe paths</h5>
080 *
081 * <p>
082 * Built-in probe paths ({@code /healthz}, {@code /readyz}, {@code /livez}) are exempted from throttling by
083 * default so a misconfigured limit cannot mask a healthy pod from the orchestrator.  Override via
084 * {@link Builder#exemptPaths(String...)}.
085 *
086 * <h5 class='topic'>Time source</h5>
087 *
088 * <p>
089 * Refill math uses {@link System#nanoTime()}.  This is monotonic and safe across wall-clock jumps but does not
090 * map to a calendar instant, which slightly complicates debugging when the bucket is in an unexpected state.  The
091 * nanosecond source is pluggable on {@link InMemoryStorage} (package-private constructor overload) so tests can
092 * pin the refill window with a deterministic clock instead of racing real wall-clock time; production code always
093 * goes through the single-arg constructor, which defaults to {@code System::nanoTime}.
094 *
095 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
096 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestServerRateLimitAndRequestId">REST Server — Rate-Limiting and Request-Id Propagation</a>
097 * </ul>
098 *
099 * @since 10.0.0
100 */
101@SuppressWarnings({
102   "java:S1192" // Duplicate string literals are HTTP header names and rate-limit response field names; intentional
103})
104public class RateLimitGuard extends RestGuard {
105
106   /** Response header name for the advisory ceiling (tokens per refill window). */
107   public static final String HEADER_LIMIT = "X-RateLimit-Limit";
108
109   /** Response header name for the advisory tokens remaining after this call. */
110   public static final String HEADER_REMAINING = "X-RateLimit-Remaining";
111
112   /** Response header name for the advisory seconds until the bucket is fully refilled. */
113   public static final String HEADER_RESET = "X-RateLimit-Reset";
114
115   /** Standard HTTP {@code Retry-After} header name. */
116   public static final String HEADER_RETRY_AFTER = "Retry-After";
117
118   private final int capacity;
119   private final double permitsPerSecond;
120   private final Function<RestRequest,String> keyResolver;
121   private final boolean xForwardedForAware;
122   private final Set<String> exemptPaths;
123   private final BiConsumer<RestRequest,RateLimitInfo> onLimitExceeded;
124   private final Storage storage;
125
126   /**
127    * Constructor.
128    *
129    * @param b The builder configuring this guard.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
130    */
131   protected RateLimitGuard(Builder b) {
132      assertArgNotNull("builder", b);
133      if (b.permitsPerSecond <= 0.0)
134         throw new IllegalArgumentException("Argument 'permitsPerSecond' must be > 0.");
135      if (b.burst <= 0)
136         throw new IllegalArgumentException("Argument 'burst' must be > 0.");
137      this.capacity = b.burst;
138      this.permitsPerSecond = b.permitsPerSecond;
139      this.keyResolver = b.keyResolver != null ? b.keyResolver : RestRequest::getRemoteAddr;
140      this.xForwardedForAware = b.xForwardedForAware;
141      this.exemptPaths = Set.copyOf(b.exemptPaths);
142      this.onLimitExceeded = b.onLimitExceeded;
143      this.storage = b.storage != null ? b.storage : Storage.inMemory();
144   }
145
146   /**
147    * Creates a new builder.
148    *
149    * @return A new builder.
150    */
151   public static Builder create() {
152      return new Builder();
153   }
154
155   @Override /* Overridden from RestGuard */
156   @SuppressWarnings({
157      "java:S3516" // Always returns true by design: a throttled request throws TooManyRequests (the guard's rejection signal per RestGuard's contract), so the normal-exit paths intentionally only ever return true.
158   })
159   public boolean guard(RestRequest req, RestResponse res) {
160      if (isExempt(req))
161         return true;
162      var key = resolveKey(req);
163      var result = storage.tryAcquire(key, capacity, permitsPerSecond);
164      var info = new RateLimitInfo(key, capacity, result.remaining(), result.secondsUntilReset(), result.allowed());
165      if (! result.allowed()) {
166         setAdvisoryHeaders(res, info);
167         var retry = Math.max(1L, info.secondsUntilReset());
168         res.setHeader(HEADER_RETRY_AFTER, Long.toString(retry));
169         if (onLimitExceeded != null)
170            onLimitExceeded.accept(req, info);
171         throw tooManyRequests(info);
172      }
173      setAdvisoryHeaders(res, info);
174      return true;
175   }
176
177   @Override /* Overridden from RestGuard */
178   @SuppressWarnings({
179      "java:S3516" // Always returns true by design: throttling is enforced in the overridden guard() method, so this abstract-contract method intentionally never rejects on its own.
180   })
181   public boolean isRequestAllowed(RestRequest req) {
182      return true;
183   }
184
185   private boolean isExempt(RestRequest req) {
186      if (exemptPaths.isEmpty())
187         return false;
188      var pi = Objects.toString(req.getPathInfo(), "");
189      var sp = Objects.toString(req.getServletPath(), "");
190      return exemptPaths.contains(pi) || exemptPaths.contains(sp);
191   }
192
193   private String resolveKey(RestRequest req) {
194      if (xForwardedForAware) {
195         var xff = req.getHeader("X-Forwarded-For");
196         if (xff != null && ! xff.isBlank()) {
197            var comma = xff.indexOf(',');
198            return (comma < 0 ? xff : xff.substring(0, comma)).trim();
199         }
200      }
201      var k = keyResolver.apply(req);
202      return or(k, "");
203   }
204
205   private static TooManyRequests tooManyRequests(RateLimitInfo info) {
206      var retry = Math.max(1L, info.secondsUntilReset());
207      var ex = new TooManyRequests("Rate limit exceeded for key '%s'. Retry after %ss.", info.key(), retry);
208      ex.setHeader(HEADER_LIMIT, Integer.toString(info.limit()));
209      ex.setHeader(HEADER_REMAINING, "0");
210      ex.setHeader(HEADER_RESET, Long.toString(info.secondsUntilReset()));
211      ex.setHeader(HEADER_RETRY_AFTER, Long.toString(retry));
212      return ex;
213   }
214
215   private static void setAdvisoryHeaders(RestResponse res, RateLimitInfo info) {
216      res.setHeader(HEADER_LIMIT, Integer.toString(info.limit()));
217      res.setHeader(HEADER_REMAINING, Integer.toString(info.remaining()));
218      res.setHeader(HEADER_RESET, Long.toString(info.secondsUntilReset()));
219   }
220
221   /**
222    * Builder for {@link RateLimitGuard}.
223    */
224   public static class Builder {
225
226      private static final Set<String> DEFAULT_EXEMPT_PATHS = Set.of("/healthz", "/readyz", "/livez");
227
228      double permitsPerSecond = 10.0;
229      int burst = 10;
230      Function<RestRequest,String> keyResolver;
231      boolean xForwardedForAware;
232      Set<String> exemptPaths = new LinkedHashSet<>(DEFAULT_EXEMPT_PATHS);
233      BiConsumer<RestRequest,RateLimitInfo> onLimitExceeded;
234      Storage storage;
235
236      /**
237       * Constructor.
238       */
239      protected Builder() {}
240
241      /**
242       * Sets the steady-state refill rate in permits per second.
243       *
244       * @param value Permits per second.  Must be {@code > 0}.
245       * @return This object.
246       */
247      public Builder permitsPerSecond(int value) {
248         permitsPerSecond = value;
249         return this;
250      }
251
252      /**
253       * Sets the steady-state refill rate in permits per minute.
254       *
255       * <p>
256       * Equivalent to {@code permitsPerSecond(value / 60.0)}.
257       *
258       * @param value Permits per minute.  Must be {@code > 0}.
259       * @return This object.
260       */
261      public Builder permitsPerMinute(int value) {
262         permitsPerSecond = value / 60.0;
263         return this;
264      }
265
266      /**
267       * Sets the steady-state refill rate in permits per hour.
268       *
269       * <p>
270       * Equivalent to {@code permitsPerSecond(value / 3600.0)}.
271       *
272       * @param value Permits per hour.  Must be {@code > 0}.
273       * @return This object.
274       */
275      public Builder permitsPerHour(int value) {
276         permitsPerSecond = value / 3600.0;
277         return this;
278      }
279
280      /**
281       * Sets the burst capacity (maximum tokens a bucket can hold).
282       *
283       * @param value Burst capacity.  Must be {@code > 0}.
284       * @return This object.
285       */
286      public Builder burst(int value) {
287         burst = value;
288         return this;
289      }
290
291      /**
292       * Sets the per-request key resolver.
293       *
294       * <p>
295       * Default is {@link RestRequest#getRemoteAddr()}.  Common alternatives include the user-principal name,
296       * an API-key header, or a tenant id.  When the resolver returns <jk>null</jk> the empty string is used.
297       *
298       * @param value Resolver function.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
299       * @return This object.
300       */
301      public Builder keyBy(Function<RestRequest,String> value) {
302         assertArgNotNull("value", value);
303         keyResolver = value;
304         return this;
305      }
306
307      /**
308       * Enables {@code X-Forwarded-For}-aware key resolution.
309       *
310       * <p>
311       * When enabled, the first comma-separated hop of the {@code X-Forwarded-For} header takes precedence over
312       * the configured {@link #keyBy(Function)} resolver.  Only opt in when a trusted reverse proxy strips and
313       * rewrites the header; otherwise clients can spoof it to defeat IP-based throttling.
314       *
315       * @param value <jk>true</jk> to honor {@code X-Forwarded-For}.
316       * @return This object.
317       */
318      public Builder xForwardedForAware(boolean value) {
319         xForwardedForAware = value;
320         return this;
321      }
322
323      /**
324       * Sets the set of request paths that bypass throttling.
325       *
326       * <p>
327       * Matched against {@link RestRequest#getPathInfo()} and {@link RestRequest#getServletPath()} (exact
328       * match).  Defaults to {@code /healthz}, {@code /readyz}, {@code /livez} — the built-in probe paths.
329       * Pass an empty array to clear the defaults.
330       *
331       * @param values Exempt paths.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
332       * @return This object.
333       */
334      public Builder exemptPaths(String...values) {
335         assertArgNotNull("values", values);
336         exemptPaths = new LinkedHashSet<>(Arrays.asList(values));
337         return this;
338      }
339
340      /**
341       * Sets a callback invoked when a request is rejected due to an empty bucket.
342       *
343       * <p>
344       * Useful for structured logging or metrics emission.  The callback runs before {@link TooManyRequests} is
345       * thrown and must not block.  Exceptions raised inside the callback propagate to the caller.
346       *
347       * @param value Callback.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
348       * @return This object.
349       */
350      public Builder whenLimitExceeded(BiConsumer<RestRequest,RateLimitInfo> value) {
351         assertArgNotNull("value", value);
352         onLimitExceeded = value;
353         return this;
354      }
355
356      /**
357       * Sets the bucket-state storage backend.
358       *
359       * <p>
360       * Default is {@link Storage#inMemory()}.  Substitute a distributed backend (Redis, DynamoDB, etc.) when
361       * running multiple pods that share a single rate envelope.
362       *
363       * @param value Storage backend.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
364       * @return This object.
365       */
366      public Builder storage(Storage value) {
367         assertArgNotNull("value", value);
368         storage = value;
369         return this;
370      }
371
372      /**
373       * Builds the guard.
374       *
375       * @return A new {@link RateLimitGuard}.
376       */
377      public RateLimitGuard build() {
378         return new RateLimitGuard(this);
379      }
380   }

382   /**
383    * Snapshot of rate-limit state passed to the {@link Builder#whenLimitExceeded(BiConsumer) onLimitExceeded}
384    * callback and used to populate advisory response headers.
385    *
386    * @param key The per-request key (e.g. remote address, principal name).
387    * @param limit The bucket capacity (also reported as {@code X-RateLimit-Limit}).
388    * @param remaining Tokens remaining after this acquisition attempt.  Zero when the request was rejected.
389    * @param secondsUntilReset Seconds until the bucket is full again (also reported as {@code X-RateLimit-Reset}).
390    * @param allowed <jk>true</jk> if the request was admitted; <jk>false</jk> if the bucket was empty.
391    */
392   public record RateLimitInfo(String key, int limit, int remaining, long secondsUntilReset, boolean allowed) {}
393
394   /**
395    * Point-in-time view of a single token bucket as exposed by {@link Storage#snapshot()}.
396    *
397    * <p>
398    * Used by operator-facing tooling (e.g. {@code AdminMixin}'s {@code /admin/ratelimit} endpoint) to
399    * surface live per-key bucket state alongside the static configuration.  Token-bucket vocabulary
400    * intentionally — there is no discrete refill window because the bucket refills continuously at
401    * {@code permitsPerSecond}, so this record reports the current fill level ({@link #tokens()}), the integer
402    * tokens currently available ({@link #remaining()}), a convenience throttled flag, and the wall-clock instant
403    * of the bucket's last activity.
404    *
405    * @param key The per-request key (e.g. remote address, principal name).
406    * @param tokens The current fractional token count in the bucket.  Continuously refilled at the
407    *    configured {@code permitsPerSecond} rate up to the configured capacity.
408    * @param remaining The integer number of tokens currently available — {@code floor(tokens)}.
409    *    Mirrors the {@code X-RateLimit-Remaining} advisory header.
410    * @param throttled <jk>true</jk> when the bucket is empty enough that the next request would be rejected
411    *    ({@code tokens < 1.0}).  Convenience flag for at-a-glance operator dashboards.
412    * @param lastRequest The wall-clock {@link Instant} at which the bucket was last touched.
413    *
414    * @since 10.0.0
415    */
416   public record BucketState(String key, double tokens, int remaining, boolean throttled, Instant lastRequest) {}
417
418   /**
419    * Returns the bucket capacity (the maximum number of tokens a bucket can hold).
420    *
421    * @return The bucket capacity.
422    * @since 10.0.0
423    */
424   public int getCapacity() {
425      return capacity;
426   }

434   public double getPermitsPerSecond() {

444   public boolean isXForwardedForAware() {

459    * Returns the bucket-state storage backend in use by this guard.
460    *

464   public Storage getStorage() {

468   /**
469    * Convenience accessor for {@link Storage#snapshot()} on the underlying storage backend.
470    *
471    * <p>
472    * Returns an empty map when the configured {@link Storage} does not override
473    * {@link Storage#snapshot()} (the default behavior for storages — e.g. Redis-backed — that can't cheaply
474    * enumerate every bucket).
475    *
476    * @return A point-in-time map of per-key bucket state.  Never <jk>null</jk>.
477    * @since 10.0.0
478    */
479   public Map<String,BucketState> snapshot() {
480      return storage.snapshot();
481   }
482
483   /**
484    * SPI for storing per-key token-bucket state.
485    *
486    * <p>
487    * Implementations must be thread-safe.  The default {@link #inMemory()} implementation is suitable for
488    * single-pod deployments.  Multi-pod deployments that share a single rate envelope should substitute a
489    * distributed backend.
490    *
491    * @since 10.0.0
492    */
493   public interface Storage {
494
495      /**
496       * Attempts to acquire one token from the bucket associated with the given key.
497       *
498       * @param key The bucket key.  Never <jk>null</jk>.
499       * @param capacity The maximum tokens the bucket can hold.
500       * @param permitsPerSecond The steady-state refill rate.
501       * @return The outcome of the attempt.  Never <jk>null</jk>.
502       */
503      AcquireResult tryAcquire(String key, int capacity, double permitsPerSecond);
504
505      /**
506       * Evicts buckets idle for longer than the given TTL.
507       *
508       * <p>
509       * The default {@link #inMemory()} implementation evicts opportunistically when its size cap is exceeded;
510       * call this method to force an eager sweep (typically from a scheduled task).
511       *
512       * @param ttl The idle threshold.  Buckets last touched longer than {@code ttl} ago are removed.
513       */
514      void evict(Duration ttl);
515
516      /**
517       * Returns a point-in-time view of every per-key bucket currently held by this storage backend.
518       *
519       * <p>
520       * Optional operation for operational visibility.  The default implementation returns an empty map so
521       * that external storage backends (Redis, DynamoDB, etc.) that can't cheaply enumerate every bucket
522       * stay backwards-compatible without code changes.  In-memory implementations <b>SHOULD</b> override
523       * this to expose live bucket state — see the bundled {@link #inMemory()} implementation, which walks
524       * its internal map and returns one {@link BucketState} per entry.
525       *
526       * <p>
527       * The returned map is a snapshot, not a live view — concurrent modifications to the underlying
528       * storage after this method returns are not reflected.  Per-bucket reads are individually consistent
529       * (the in-memory implementation reads each bucket under its own monitor), but the snapshot as a whole
530       * is not a global point-in-time consistent view.
531       *
532       * <p>
533       * <b>Cardinality warning:</b> on storages that hold many buckets (the bundled in-memory storage caps
534       * at 100&nbsp;000 keys by default) the returned map can be large.  Operator-facing callers should
535       * either filter client-side or use a paginated alternative if one is offered by the backend.
536       *
537       * @return A point-in-time map of per-key bucket state, keyed by per-request key.  Never <jk>null</jk>.
538       * @since 10.0.0
539       */
540      default Map<String,BucketState> snapshot() {
541         return Map.of();
542      }
543
544      /**
545       * Creates a new in-memory storage backend with the default size cap (100 000 keys).
546       *
547       * @return A new in-memory storage backend.
548       */
549      static Storage inMemory() {
550         return new InMemoryStorage(100_000);
551      }
552
553      /**
554       * Creates a new in-memory storage backend with a custom size cap.
555       *
556       * @param maxKeys The maximum number of keys held before LRU-style eviction kicks in.  Must be {@code > 0}.
557       * @return A new in-memory storage backend.
558       */
559      static Storage inMemory(int maxKeys) {
560         return new InMemoryStorage(maxKeys);
561      }
562
563      /**
564       * Outcome of a {@link #tryAcquire(String, int, double) tryAcquire} attempt.
565       *
566       * @param allowed <jk>true</jk> if the request was admitted.
567       * @param remaining Tokens left in the bucket after the attempt.
568       * @param secondsUntilReset Seconds until the bucket is full again.
569       */
570      record AcquireResult(boolean allowed, int remaining, long secondsUntilReset) {}
571   }
572
573   /**
574    * Default in-memory {@link Storage} implementation.
575    *
576    * <p>
577    * Backed by a {@link ConcurrentHashMap} keyed by the per-request key.  Each bucket tracks token count and last
578    * touch time.  When the map exceeds {@code maxKeys} entries the least-recently-touched bucket is removed.
579    */
580   static final class InMemoryStorage implements Storage {
581
582      private final ConcurrentHashMap<String,Bucket> buckets = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
583      private final int maxKeys;
584      private final LongSupplier nanoClock;
585
586      InMemoryStorage(int maxKeys) {
587         this(maxKeys, System::nanoTime);
588      }
589
590      /**
591       * Constructor allowing the nanosecond time source to be overridden.
592       *
593       * <p>
594       * Test-only seam.  Production code should always use {@link #InMemoryStorage(int)}, which defaults to
595       * real {@link System#nanoTime()}.  Tests that need to pin the token-bucket refill window regardless of
596       * machine speed can supply a deterministic {@link LongSupplier} here instead of racing {@link Thread#sleep}
597       * against real time.
598       *
599       * @param maxKeys The maximum number of keys held before LRU-style eviction kicks in.  Must be {@code > 0}.
600       * @param nanoClock Supplies the current time in nanoseconds for refill math and idle-eviction bookkeeping.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
601       */
602      InMemoryStorage(int maxKeys, LongSupplier nanoClock) {
603         assertArgNotNull("nanoClock", nanoClock);
604         if (maxKeys <= 0)
605            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Argument 'maxKeys' must be > 0.");
606         this.maxKeys = maxKeys;
607         this.nanoClock = nanoClock;
608      }
609
610      @Override
611      public AcquireResult tryAcquire(String key, int capacity, double permitsPerSecond) {
612         var bucket = buckets.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> new Bucket(capacity, nanoClock));
613         var result = bucket.tryAcquire(capacity, permitsPerSecond);
614         if (buckets.size() > maxKeys)
615            evictOldest();
616         return result;
617      }
618
619      @Override
620      public void evict(Duration ttl) {
621         var threshold = nanoClock.getAsLong() - ttl.toNanos();
622         buckets.entrySet().removeIf(e -> e.getValue().lastTouchedNanos() < threshold);
623      }
624
625      @Override
626      public Map<String,BucketState> snapshot() {
627         var out = new LinkedHashMap<String,BucketState>();
628         for (var e : buckets.entrySet()) {
629            var b = e.getValue();
630            var tokens = b.tokens();
631            out.put(e.getKey(), new BucketState(
632               e.getKey(),
633               tokens,
634               (int) Math.floor(tokens),
635               tokens < 1.0,
636               Instant.ofEpochMilli(b.lastWallMillis())
637            ));
638         }
639         return Map.copyOf(out);
640      }
641
642      int size() {
643         return buckets.size();
644      }
645
646      private void evictOldest() {
647         buckets.entrySet().stream()
648            .min(Comparator.comparingLong(e -> e.getValue().lastTouchedNanos()))
649            .map(Map.Entry::getKey)
650            .ifPresent(buckets::remove);
651      }
652   }
653
654   /**
655    * Per-key token-bucket state.
656    *
657    * <p>
658    * Holds a fractional token count and the {@link System#nanoTime()} value of the last touch.  The
659    * {@code synchronized} block keeps the read-refill-write sequence atomic without the overhead of a lock-free
660    * CAS loop on this hot path.
661    */
662   static final class Bucket {
663
664      private double tokens;
665      private long lastNanos;
666      private long lastWallMillis;
667      private final LongSupplier nanoClock;
668
669      Bucket(int capacity) {
670         this(capacity, System::nanoTime);
671      }
672
673      /**
674       * Constructor allowing the nanosecond time source to be overridden.
675       *
676       * <p>
677       * Test-only seam — see {@link InMemoryStorage#InMemoryStorage(int, LongSupplier)}.
678       *
679       * @param capacity The initial (full) token count.
680       * @param nanoClock Supplies the current time in nanoseconds for refill math.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
681       */
682      Bucket(int capacity, LongSupplier nanoClock) {
683         this.nanoClock = nanoClock;
684         this.tokens = capacity;
685         this.lastNanos = nanoClock.getAsLong();
686         this.lastWallMillis = System.currentTimeMillis();
687      }
688
689      synchronized Storage.AcquireResult tryAcquire(int capacity, double permitsPerSecond) {
690         var now = nanoClock.getAsLong();
691         var elapsedSeconds = (now - lastNanos) / 1_000_000_000.0;
692         tokens = Math.min(capacity, tokens + elapsedSeconds * permitsPerSecond);
693         lastNanos = now;
694         lastWallMillis = System.currentTimeMillis();
695         if (tokens >= 1.0) {
696            tokens -= 1.0;
697            return new Storage.AcquireResult(true, (int) Math.floor(tokens), secondsUntilFull(capacity, permitsPerSecond));
698         }
699         return new Storage.AcquireResult(false, 0, secondsUntilFull(capacity, permitsPerSecond));
700      }
701
702      synchronized long lastTouchedNanos() {
703         return lastNanos;
704      }
705
706      synchronized double tokens() {
707         return tokens;
708      }
709
710      synchronized long lastWallMillis() {
711         return lastWallMillis;
712      }
713
714      private long secondsUntilFull(int capacity, double permitsPerSecond) {
715         var needed = Math.max(0.0, capacity - tokens);
716         return (long) Math.ceil(needed / permitsPerSecond);
717      }
718   }
719}
